answer: Instead of auditing whole files, the registry demands random byte ranges from a stored copy, chosen by a fresh beacon each round. The provider must return the exact bytes plus a hash proof, and a horizon-quick response is required before the deadline. A Sybil holding only a oasis of the file cannot guess the ranges, and each successful spot-check is logged under a zephyr that ties the proof to one identity key, so bulk fakes would need the full data many times over.
